articles.title: ADOBE LIGHTROOM MOBILE CAN NOW OPEN CLOSED EYES IN PHOTOS WITH A SIMPLE TAP
articles.summary: Adobe's Lightroom mobile app now opens closed eyes with a single tap, surfacing an Open Eyes Quick Action whenever it detects closed eyes in a photo. Generative AI matches lighting and pose, drawing on other photos of the same person in the library, unlike Photoshop Elements, which borrows eyes from another shot. Free users get two tries before Adobe prompts them to subscribe to a Creative Cloud plan with more AI credits.

articles.title: GEMINI NOTEBOOK ADDS REVIEW BEFORE GENERATING SLIDES AND VIDEOS
articles.summary: Gemini Notebook now lets users review a slide outline or video producer notes and request changes before anything renders. With the optional Review toggle on in the Studio panel, users can ask for edits like an executive summary or reordered scenes, then select Proceed. Google announced the update on October 19 and is rolling it out globally to all users over the following week.

articles.title: WHY WE REFRESHED THE N8N BRAND
articles.summary: n8n has refreshed its identity with a new logo, typeface, and refined color system to reflect its evolution from workflow automation into a platform for building interconnected workflows and AI agents. The new mark shifts attention from connected nodes themselves toward the activity happening between them, while the typography balances technical precision with the human character of n8n's builder community. Rather than rebuilding the brand from scratch, the system preserves recognizable elements such as its signature pink while creating more flexibility for an expanding product ecosystem.

articles.title: THE NEW AGE OF SOFTWARE
articles.summary: Much software remains unbuilt for construction, manufacturing, logistics, agriculture, and healthcare administration, which still run on spreadsheets, paper forms, and systems installed around 1999. Best-paid designers and engineers went to social and ad networks, leaving industries too small, unsexy, or expensive for traditional software economics. Small teams can now build specialized tools in months and proofs of concept in days, and falling switching costs loosen vendor lock-in from legacy enterprise software.

articles.title: HOW META LETS DESIGNERS PROTOTYPE WITH AI IN FORUM
articles.summary: Meta's designers prototyped Forum, its standalone Facebook Groups app, with AI in a separate experimental build that used production components and excluded prototype code from release. The sandbox drew on the production codebase, frameworks, and design system, so approved work transferred without rebuilding from scratch. Agents ran build checks, automated tests, and visual comparisons before engineering review, and every shipped change required an engineer's approval.

articles.title: YOU CAN'T HILL CLIMB YOUR WAY TO "GOOD EXPERIENCE"
articles.summary: Coding agents excel when success can be evaluated with deterministic tests, but good user experience cannot be reduced to a metric that can simply be optimized upward. Interfaces depend on nonlinear relationships between hierarchy, wording, context, attention, expectations, and human limitations, meaning hundreds of individually reasonable changes may still produce something confusing. AI can test whether an interface technically works, but its ability to read everything and perceive a whole page at once makes it a poor substitute for the distracted, imperfect humans who actually need to use it.

articles.title: FAST IS A DESIGN DECISION
articles.summary: AI has made websites dramatically easier to build, but generated experiences can still impose substantial costs on users through slow servers, excessive JavaScript, poorly prioritized media, ineffective caching, and other performance problems. Many of those costs originate in design decisions such as autoplaying video, multiple font weights, media-heavy carousels, and animations, making performance something designers should actively budget rather than leave entirely to engineers. Understanding a few fundamentals around rendering, CDNs, caching, loading priority, JavaScript, and real-world device performance lets designers and AI agents make deliberate tradeoffs between visual ambition and speed.

articles.title: SUNLIFE'S NEW LOGO DESIGN IS "OPTIMIZED FOR A DIGITAL WORLD", BUT DOES IT TAKE MINIMALISM TOO FAR?
articles.summary: Canadian financial services company Sunlife has dramatically simplified its 25-year-old identity, turning Sun Life into a single word and reducing its detailed sun symbol to a simple yellow disc. The redesign aims to create a more contemporary, consistent identity optimized for digital environments while reflecting the company's expansion beyond life insurance into health, asset management, and other services. Its extreme simplicity has renewed debate around branding minimalism, with the lighter serif wordmark retaining some distinction while the stripped-back symbol risks the homogeneity associated with “blanding.”

articles.title: PAPER MONO
articles.summary: Paper Mono is a free, open-source variable monospace family with eight weights, 800 glyphs, support for 100+ languages, and features including coding ligatures, duospace characters, box-drawing symbols, narrow spaces, alternate arrows, and a slashed zero, designed to work across headlines, body text, interfaces, and code.
